reason: Defects: (1) No null arm and no planted-growth positive control; a constant law fits any flat data, and a slow law (log n, n/ord_n(2)) cannot be excluded on 9 odd-prime n in 13..45 without a power analysis; MDL 5-bit margin depends on grammar prior and ~5 fit n-values x 3 l. Fit set n<=29 gives only n=13,17,19,23,29; held-out 31,37,41,43. (2) Measurement mismatch: msolve -v2 F4 degree is a solving-degree witness, not the closure-certified last fall degree d_F; hky_last_fall_degree (prebuilt) already outputs certified d_last/ffd/closure_dims and needs no msolve; mixing the two defines the target inconsistently. (3) Runtime: measured hky_last_fall_degree n=13 x3 draws 0.2 s, but n=31 x3 draws cmax=8 did not finish in 120 s (killed); 30 subspaces x 3 l x 9 n of n>=31 certification will exceed the 18 CPU-min budget, so the stated cpu_minutes is unsupported. Also internally inconsistent ranges (regenerate n=13..25 vs fit n<=29). (4) Scope: tool cells use nprime~n/2 (n=13 -> nprime 6) at m=2; stated l in {3,4,5} is unclear against that convention, and the open lever cells are m>=3 (4,4),(4,5),(4,6). Since closure gives d_F<=k+2 (k tied to subspace dim), growth in l is already bounded-by-theorem and growth in n at fixed l is the only informative axis; m=2 binary S_3 at fixed small l saturates near the bound and says nothing about l~n/m growth needed at n=131. (5) Metric is structural (degrees, ranks), not wall time: good. Result is toy-only: a flat-in-n law at fixed small l does not imply a poly oracle at n=131 because required l grows with n; classification stays accounting; B*D^2<<N unaffected. Censored lower bounds (cmax truncation) make 'residual>=1' undefined unless censoring is encoded as inequality.
fix: Redesign: (a) Target = certified d_last from hky_last_fall_degree (ffd and d_last both recorded), drop msolve for this target; use msolve -v2 only as an independent cross-check of the F4 solving degree on <=3 cells/n. (b) Axes: fix l in {3,4,5} absolute AND a second family with l=ceil(n/m) (m=2, tool's native nprime) so extrapolation in n at growing l is tested; theory bound k+2 is the comparator law. (c) Budget: per-n cap with timeout; n=13..29 full (30 draws), n=31..43 only 5 draws/cell with --cmax = bound+1; report cost log; if n>=37 not certifiable in budget declare them censored and score only certified cells; encode censored cells as d_F>=c inequality in the fit (hinge loss), never as equality. (d) Null/controls: random_matched system per cell (ffd_semaev_core.random_matched) as null arm; synthetic planted datasets with identical grid and noise: d=const, d=4+floor((l-2)/4), d=ceil(log2 n), d=l+2, to measure the grammar search power (false-bounded rate on log-n planted law must be reported; require held-out-n distinguishing power >=90% before using result). (e) Pre-register grammar, fit set n in {13,17,19,23,29}, held-out {31,37,41,43}, MDL = integer-valued likelihood + structural code length, and decision rule: bounded iff best law has no n or l term AND planted log-n law is rejected at the same grid. (f) Report the result as a toy statement about presentation features (l, ord_n(2), subspace type) only; add explicit non-claim that no extrapolation to n=131 follows, and that lever 1 stays open unless a pseudo-solution (certificate) proof accompanies it. Expected class remains accounting.
